details.description: Gemini 3.5 Flash is Google DeepMind's Flash-tier model in the Gemini 3 reasoning series, built on Gemini 3 Flash with adjustable thinking levels to balance response quality, latency and cost. It is natively multimodal, accepting text, image, audio and video input over up to a 1M-token context window, and is positioned for agentic workflows, coding and long-running enterprise tasks. Google's own developer documentation now describes it as "our legacy Flash model, providing baseline speed and foundational performance for routine, high-throughput workloads."
advantages: Scores 83.6% on the agentic MCP Atlas benchmark and 56.5% on Toolathlon, per its Google DeepMind model card.
Scores 76.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 55.1% on SWE-Bench Pro for coding tasks.
Scores 83.6% on MMMU-Pro and 84.2% on CharXiv for multimodal reasoning over images.
Scores 72.1% on ARC-AGI-2, a general reasoning benchmark.
Offers adjustable thinking levels to trade off response quality against latency and cost.
disadvantages: Google's developer docs now describe it as their legacy Flash model, providing baseline speed and foundational performance for routine, high-throughput workloads.
Scores only 26.6% on the MRCR v2 (1M) long-context benchmark cited on its model card.
use_cases: Agentic workflows that call tools across multi-step tasks
Multimodal reasoning over text, images, audio and video
Routine, high-throughput chat workloads where Google positions it as the baseline Flash option

notes: Catalog facts (1,048,576 input tokens, 65,536 output tokens, audio+image+text input) match the DeepMind model card, which also mentions video file input that the catalog's modality list does not include. The catalog's deprecation date (2027-05-19) was not confirmed on any page opened; Google's own docs instead call this model 'legacy', without giving a retirement date. As of 2026-09-24, ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models also lists newer stable Flash models (3.6, 3.7, and 3.8 Flash) beyond the 3.5 Flash-Lite/3.6 Flash pairing originally noted, so no specific successor model is named in the description. Knowledge cutoff was not stated on the pages opened; the model card defers limitations/safety details to the Gemini 3 Flash model card rather than listing them itself. The 'Long context' evaluation is officially named 'MRCR v2 (1M)' on the source page; renamed to match. Verified against the model card's benchmark table that all evaluation scores belong to the Gemini 3.5 Flash column specifically, not a sibling model shown in the same comparison table.
